chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the geometry of the central carbon in an SN2 transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: Tetrahedral with retention of configuration

options.label: B
options.text: Trigonal bipyramidal with incoming nucleophile and departing leaving group at 180°

options.label: C
options.text: Linear with sp hybridization

options.label: D
options.text: Planar carbocation with 120° bond angles

questions.correct_answer: Trigonal bipyramidal with incoming nucleophile and departing leaving group at 180°
questions.explanation: The central carbon in an SN2 transition state is pentacoordinate in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement with 180° inversion axis.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which step is rate-determining in the SN1 solvolysis of tert-butyl bromide?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprotonation of the oxonium ion intermediate

options.label: B
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of solvent on the carbocation

options.label: C
options.text: Diffusion of ions in polar solvent

options.label: D
options.text: Heterolytic cleavage of the C-Br bond to form the tert-butyl carbocation

questions.correct_answer: Heterolytic cleavage of the C-Br bond to form the tert-butyl carbocation
questions.explanation: The highest activation barrier in SN1 is unimolecular bond ionization to generate the high-energy carbocation.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why does E2 elimination require an anti-periplanar conformation between the beta-hydrogen and leaving group?

options.label: A
options.text: It minimizes electrostatic attraction between base and leaving group

options.label: B
options.text: It forces the reaction to proceed through a planar carbocation

options.label: C
options.text: It prevents syn-addition of solvent molecules

options.label: D
options.text: It allows optimal continuous orbital overlap between the C-H sigma and C-X sigma* orbitals to form the developing pi bond

questions.correct_answer: It allows optimal continuous orbital overlap between the C-H sigma and C-X sigma* orbitals to form the developing pi bond
questions.explanation: Anti-coplanar alignment maximizes overlap between the breaking sigma bonds and the developing pi system.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: How does the E1 mechanism differ from the E2 mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: E1 requires a strong base; E2 requires a weak base

options.label: B
options.text: E1 occurs with anti-periplanar stereospecificity; E2 does not

options.label: C
options.text: E1 is stepwise through a carbocation intermediate; E2 is concerted in a single step

options.label: D
options.text: E1 is bimolecular; E2 is unimolecular

questions.correct_answer: E1 is stepwise through a carbocation intermediate; E2 is concerted in a single step
questions.explanation: E1 involves unimolecular rate-determining ionization, whereas E2 involves concerted bimolecular elimination.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What reactive intermediate is generated in the first step of an E1cB elimination?

options.label: A
options.text: A free radical intermediate

options.label: B
options.text: A resonance-stabilized carbanion conjugate base

options.label: C
options.text: A cyclic bromonium ion

options.label: D
options.text: A planar carbocation

questions.correct_answer: A resonance-stabilized carbanion conjugate base
questions.explanation: In E1cB, a base removes an acidic proton to form a stabilized carbanion, which subsequently expels the leaving group.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What causes the complete stereochemical inversion in an SN2 substitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Planarization of the carbocation intermediate

options.label: B
options.text: Rapid equilibrium between enantiomers

options.label: C
options.text: Backside attack of the nucleophile opposite to the departing leaving group

options.label: D
options.text: Frontside attack with retention of configuration

questions.correct_answer: Backside attack of the nucleophile opposite to the departing leaving group
questions.explanation: Nucleophile must attack the back lobe of the C-LG sigma* antibonding orbital, inverting tetrahedral geometry.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why do polar aprotic solvents (like DMSO and DMF) dramatically accelerate SN2 reactions?

options.label: A
options.text: They protonate the leaving group to make it better

options.label: B
options.text: They stabilize the planar carbocation intermediate

options.label: C
options.text: They solvate metal cations strongly while leaving anions 'naked' and highly nucleophilic

options.label: D
options.text: They decrease the reaction temperature requirement

questions.correct_answer: They solvate metal cations strongly while leaving anions 'naked' and highly nucleophilic
questions.explanation: Polar aprotic solvents lack hydrogen-bonding protons, preventing solvent cages around nucleophilic anions.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why is iodide (I-) a much better leaving group than fluoride (F-)?

options.label: A
options.text: Iodide is insoluble in polar solvents

options.label: B
options.text: Iodide forms stronger covalent bonds with carbon

options.label: C
options.text: Iodide has higher electronegativity than fluoride

options.label: D
options.text: Iodide is the weak conjugate base of a strong acid with a large polarizable ionic radius

questions.correct_answer: Iodide is the weak conjugate base of a strong acid with a large polarizable ionic radius
questions.explanation: Good leaving groups are weak bases that stabilize negative charge over large, polarizable electron clouds.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why does the E2 elimination of 2-bromobutane with ethoxide favor 2-butene over 1-butene?

options.label: A
options.text: 1-Butene is more sterically crowded than 2-butene

options.label: B
options.text: The transition state leading to 2-butene has greater partial double-bond character and is more stable due to alkyl hyperconjugation

options.label: C
options.text: Ethoxide is too bulky to attack the secondary carbon

options.label: D
options.text: 2-Butene is formed by an SN1 pathway

questions.correct_answer: The transition state leading to 2-butene has greater partial double-bond character and is more stable due to alkyl hyperconjugation
questions.explanation: The transition state resembles the more substituted, lower-energy alkene product (Zaitsev's rule).

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What mechanistic phenomenon frequently complicates SN1 reactions of secondary alkyl halides?

options.label: A
options.text: 1,2-Hydride or 1,2-alkyl shifts to form more stable tertiary carbocations

options.label: B
options.text: Concerted backside Walden inversions

options.label: C
options.text: Anti-periplanar stereospecific eliminations

options.label: D
options.text: Radical disproportionation

questions.correct_answer: 1,2-Hydride or 1,2-alkyl shifts to form more stable tertiary carbocations
questions.explanation: Once formed, 2° carbocations readily rearrange to 3° carbocations before nucleophilic capture.

questions.question: Why does the E2 elimination of 2-bromobutane with ethoxide favor 2-butene over 1-butene?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethoxide is too bulky to attack the secondary carbon

options.label: B
options.text: The transition state leading to 2-butene has greater partial double-bond character and is more stable due to alkyl hyperconjugation

options.label: C
options.text: 2-Butene is formed by an SN1 pathway

options.label: D
options.text: 1-Butene is more sterically crowded than 2-butene

questions.correct_answer: The transition state leading to 2-butene has greater partial double-bond character and is more stable due to alkyl hyperconjugation
questions.explanation: The transition state resembles the more substituted, lower-energy alkene product (Zaitsev's rule).

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What mechanistic phenomenon frequently complicates SN1 reactions of secondary alkyl halides?

options.label: A
options.text: Concerted backside Walden inversions

options.label: B
options.text: 1,2-Hydride or 1,2-alkyl shifts to form more stable tertiary carbocations

options.label: C
options.text: Anti-periplanar stereospecific eliminations

options.label: D
options.text: Radical disproportionation

questions.correct_answer: 1,2-Hydride or 1,2-alkyl shifts to form more stable tertiary carbocations
questions.explanation: Once formed, 2° carbocations readily rearrange to 3° carbocations before nucleophilic capture.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the geometry of the central carbon in an SN2 transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: Planar carbocation with 120° bond angles

options.label: B
options.text: Trigonal bipyramidal with incoming nucleophile and departing leaving group at 180°

options.label: C
options.text: Tetrahedral with retention of configuration

options.label: D
options.text: Linear with sp hybridization

questions.correct_answer: Trigonal bipyramidal with incoming nucleophile and departing leaving group at 180°
questions.explanation: The central carbon in an SN2 transition state is pentacoordinate in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement with 180° inversion axis.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which step is rate-determining in the SN1 solvolysis of tert-butyl bromide?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprotonation of the oxonium ion intermediate

options.label: B
options.text: Heterolytic cleavage of the C-Br bond to form the tert-butyl carbocation

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of solvent on the carbocation

options.label: D
options.text: Diffusion of ions in polar solvent

questions.correct_answer: Heterolytic cleavage of the C-Br bond to form the tert-butyl carbocation
questions.explanation: The highest activation barrier in SN1 is unimolecular bond ionization to generate the high-energy carbocation.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why does E2 elimination require an anti-periplanar conformation between the beta-hydrogen and leaving group?

options.label: A
options.text: It prevents syn-addition of solvent molecules

options.label: B
options.text: It allows optimal continuous orbital overlap between the C-H sigma and C-X sigma* orbitals to form the developing pi bond

options.label: C
options.text: It forces the reaction to proceed through a planar carbocation

options.label: D
options.text: It minimizes electrostatic attraction between base and leaving group

questions.correct_answer: It allows optimal continuous orbital overlap between the C-H sigma and C-X sigma* orbitals to form the developing pi bond
questions.explanation: Anti-coplanar alignment maximizes overlap between the breaking sigma bonds and the developing pi system.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: How does the E1 mechanism differ from the E2 mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: E1 is bimolecular; E2 is unimolecular

options.label: B
options.text: E1 occurs with anti-periplanar stereospecificity; E2 does not

options.label: C
options.text: E1 is stepwise through a carbocation intermediate; E2 is concerted in a single step

options.label: D
options.text: E1 requires a strong base; E2 requires a weak base

questions.correct_answer: E1 is stepwise through a carbocation intermediate; E2 is concerted in a single step
questions.explanation: E1 involves unimolecular rate-determining ionization, whereas E2 involves concerted bimolecular elimination.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What reactive intermediate is generated in the first step of an E1cB elimination?

options.label: A
options.text: A planar carbocation

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic bromonium ion

options.label: C
options.text: A resonance-stabilized carbanion conjugate base

options.label: D
options.text: A free radical intermediate

questions.correct_answer: A resonance-stabilized carbanion conjugate base
questions.explanation: In E1cB, a base removes an acidic proton to form a stabilized carbanion, which subsequently expels the leaving group.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What causes the complete stereochemical inversion in an SN2 substitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Rapid equilibrium between enantiomers

options.label: B
options.text: Frontside attack with retention of configuration

options.label: C
options.text: Planarization of the carbocation intermediate

options.label: D
options.text: Backside attack of the nucleophile opposite to the departing leaving group

questions.correct_answer: Backside attack of the nucleophile opposite to the departing leaving group
questions.explanation: Nucleophile must attack the back lobe of the C-LG sigma* antibonding orbital, inverting tetrahedral geometry.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why do polar aprotic solvents (like DMSO and DMF) dramatically accelerate SN2 reactions?

options.label: A
options.text: They stabilize the planar carbocation intermediate

options.label: B
options.text: They solvate metal cations strongly while leaving anions 'naked' and highly nucleophilic

options.label: C
options.text: They decrease the reaction temperature requirement

options.label: D
options.text: They protonate the leaving group to make it better

questions.correct_answer: They solvate metal cations strongly while leaving anions 'naked' and highly nucleophilic
questions.explanation: Polar aprotic solvents lack hydrogen-bonding protons, preventing solvent cages around nucleophilic anions.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Why is iodide (I-) a much better leaving group than fluoride (F-)?

options.label: A
options.text: Iodide forms stronger covalent bonds with carbon

options.label: B
options.text: Iodide is the weak conjugate base of a strong acid with a large polarizable ionic radius

options.label: C
options.text: Iodide is insoluble in polar solvents

options.label: D
options.text: Iodide has higher electronegativity than fluoride

questions.correct_answer: Iodide is the weak conjugate base of a strong acid with a large polarizable ionic radius
questions.explanation: Good leaving groups are weak bases that stabilize negative charge over large, polarizable electron clouds.
